change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage to admins that only have the VIEW scope on all groups
findings.body: `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin whose all-groups permission has only the `view` scope passes `canManage()`. `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` guards creation with `auth.groups().requireManage()` (GroupsResource.java:181), so a view-only admin can create top-level groups, or move an existing group to top level by passing an id. The V1 `canManage()` and the rule 'manage requires manage' both say this should check only `MANAGE`. The javadoc added in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 75-76) repeats the VIEW-or-MANAGE wording, so it needs the same fix. Suggested fix: `return hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE);`. `testManageAllGroups` only uses MANAGE and `testViewGroups` never tries a write, so no test catches this.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns resource UUIDs of the 'Groups' type resource, not group IDs
findings.body: Per-group resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:118-127). That method names the resource with the group id and never calls `setType`. Only the all-groups type resource (created at AdminPermissionsSchema.java:271-274) has type `Groups`. So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` visits just that one type resource. The lambda then passes `groupResource.getId()`, the internal resource UUID, to `hasPermission(groupId, ...)`. That does `findByName(server, groupId)`, which finds nothing and falls back to the all-groups evaluation. When all-groups has `view-members` or `manage-members`, the set gets the type resource's UUID, which is not a group id. Otherwise the set is empty. Callers: `UsersResource.searchForUser` sets `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, ids)` when the set is non-empty. `JpaUserProvider.groupsWithPermissionsSubquery` (JpaUserProvider.java:1059-1089) then restricts users to members of those group ids, and also requires a resource named `group.resource.<groupId>` (V1 naming). Result: an admin with all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS gets zero users from search, where before this change the post-filter by `canView(user)` returned them. `/users/count` calls `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)`, which returns 0 for an empty set, so a V2 admin who can view members of specific groups sees count 0. Pagination of search is also off, because first/max are applied before the `canView` filter. Suggested fix: for V2, enumerate groups via the resource names (or the groups themselves) and add the group id. Also make the JPA subquery work with V2 resource naming, or skip the pre-filter for V2. Please add a test for `/users/count` and for search with all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS.

findings.title: Group deletion can now throw UnsupportedOperationException when V1 and V2 features are both enabled
findings.body: The listener is registered when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is on. It calls `management(...)`, which returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is on. `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns `GroupPermissionsV2`, whose `setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (GroupPermissionsV2.java:172-175). Before this PR V2 fell back to V1 `GroupPermissions` there, so deleting a group worked. With both features enabled, `GroupRemovedEvent` now throws and the group delete would fail. Clients already throw on `ClientRemovedEvent` in that combination (ClientPermissionsV2), so this may be accepted. Is the V1+V2 combination unsupported, or should the listener skip group cleanup for V2?

findings.title: Javadoc inaccuracies in GroupPermissionEvaluator
findings.body: `requireManageMembers` (line 135) is documented as throwing when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false, but the implementation checks `canManageMembers`. The `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` javadoc (line 145) says it returns a 'Stream of IDs' but the method returns `Set<String>`. The `canManageMembers` doc says it returns true if `UserPermissionEvaluator#canManage()` is true, which is correct. The V2-only note on `canManage()` (lines 75-76) documents the VIEW-or-MANAGE behaviour reported as a bug above.

findings.title: No negative test for write access with view-only permission, and no coverage of count or all-groups members scopes
findings.body: `testViewGroups` grants VIEW on all groups but never asserts that creating a group or updating a group is still forbidden, which is how the `canManage()` problem in GroupPermissionsV2 went unnoticed. There is also no test for `/users/count` or for user search with an all-groups `view-members` or `manage-members` permission, the paths that use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`. Other nits: the double semicolon on line 68, a new file with a 2024 copyright header, and trailing whitespace at line 300.

contracts.action: Group read/manage checks routed through new GroupPermissionsV2 (canView/canManage/canViewMembers/etc.)
contracts.before_after: V1 GroupPermissions checked admin roles, then per-group `group.resource.<id>` resources. V2 checks roles, then a resource named by the group id, and falls back to the 'Groups' type resource only if it has permissions. UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission additionally requires `permission.getResourceId().equals(resource.getId())`; the group variant does not, which is harmless because only one resource is evaluated.
contracts.visible_effect: Group list, view, create and update through the admin REST API and admin UI follow the new schema. canManage() also accepts the VIEW scope (reported).
contracts.failure_mode: Wrong scope in canManage() grants write access to view-only admins (silent).

contracts.action: Users search and count call auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() unconditionally and pass the result to the user provider
contracts.before_after: Before, the V2 path got an empty set (V1 lookup by type `Group` found nothing) and relied on the post-filter. Now V2 lookup by type `Groups` finds only the type resource and returns its UUID. The JPA provider restricts by `group.resource.<id>` named resources, so V2 returns nothing (search) or 0 (count). The post-filter `userModels.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` still runs in `toRepresentation` (UsersResource.java:460).
contracts.visible_effect: An admin with all-groups view-members or manage-members sees an empty users list and count 0. Admins with only per-group permissions see a correct list but wrong counts.

contracts.action: AdminPermissions.registerListener now registers the removal listener only when the V1 feature is on
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous listener checked the feature flag on each event.
contracts.before_after: Feature flags are fixed at startup, so moving the check is equivalent for a single flag. With V1+V2 both on, group removal now reaches GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled, which throws.
contracts.visible_effect: Group delete fails with a server error when both features are enabled.
contracts.failure_mode: UnsupportedOperationException propagates out of the provider event, so the delete fails.
contracts.open_question: Is enabling V1 and V2 together supported, and should group cleanup be skipped under V2?

summary:
Two real defects in the new V2 group permissions, plus one open question and some docs and test gaps.

- **Blocker:** `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` accepts the VIEW scope, so a view-only admin passes `requireManage()` in `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` and can create top-level groups.
- **Fix:** `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` walks `findByType("Groups")`, which only matches the all-groups type resource, not per-group resources. It returns that resource's UUID instead of group ids. The JPA user search and count then return nothing for V2 admins with all-groups view-members, or 0 for the count.
- **Question:** the group-removal listener can now throw `UnsupportedOperationException` if the V1 and V2 features are both enabled.

The rest of the diff (user permission refactor, V1 group changes, schema, `ApiUtil`) reads as consistent. I did not build or run anything.
